claims.text: Google DeepMind announced an updated Gemini 3 Deep Think on 2026-02-12 as a specialized reasoning mode for science, research, and engineering problems.
The February announcement described availability through the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers and an early-access path for API use rather than broad general API availability.
Scientific and benchmark performance results in the announcement are vendor claims unless independently reproduced.

limitations: Deep Think is a specialized reasoning mode, so its results should not be generalized to the entire Gemini 3 family.
Announcement-time API availability was limited/early access.
Scientific benchmark and comparison claims are vendor-reported.
overrides.why_this_special: Provides a distinct February counterpoint to the coding-agent race: specialized frontier reasoning aimed at science, research, and engineering.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

artifact.canonical_name: Gemini 3.1 Pro / Gemini 3.1 Flash Image February API releases

claims.text: The Gemini API changelog records Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview on 2026-02-19 and a custom-tools endpoint that prioritizes user-defined tools alongside built-in execution capabilities.
The changelog records Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview (Nano Banana 2) on 2026-02-26 as a speed/high-volume image-generation release.
Performance and quality superiority claims associated with these previews remain vendor claims.

limitations: Both highlighted model identifiers were preview-stage February releases; drafting must not describe them as generally stable at that date.
The API changelog is chronology evidence and does not independently validate quality/benchmark claims.
This task combines a reasoning/tool-use model update and an image-generation model update; architecture should split their editorial roles if needed.
overrides.why_this_special: Captures the late-February evolution of the general Gemini API surface across reasoning/tool use and high-throughput image generation.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

claims.text: MiniMax announced M2.5 on 2026-02-12 with emphasis on coding, agentic tool use/search, and office/workflow tasks.
MiniMax introduced Forge on 2026-02-13 as an agent-native reinforcement-learning framework with scaffold/environment abstraction and asynchronous scheduling for large-scale agent training.
M2.5 benchmark scores, speedups, and Forge scale/throughput figures are vendor-reported claims.

limitations: M2.5 benchmark and relative-speed figures are not independently reproduced.
Forge scale statements and training-throughput claims are first-party reports.
Architecture should distinguish the public model release from the training-system story rather than imply Forge itself is a broadly available product.
overrides.why_this_special: MiniMax couples a February coding/tool-use model release with an agent-native RL framework, directly exposing how vendors were training for long-horizon software and tool environments.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

claims.text: Mistral announced the Voxtral Transcribe 2 family on 2026-02-04, including a realtime streaming speech-to-text model.
The realtime model was released as open weights under Apache 2.0 and described as a 4B-parameter streaming ASR model supporting 13 languages.
Latency, word-error-rate, and price/performance comparisons in the launch material are vendor claims.

limitations: Sub-200ms latency and accuracy comparisons are vendor-reported and depend on the stated serving configuration.
Open-weight/license status does not imply every surrounding hosted service component is open source.
The task source is Mistral’s news index; item-level wording must remain consistent with the February launch article.
overrides.why_this_special: Voxtral Realtime makes realtime speech a concrete February systems/model axis, broadening the Special beyond text-centric coding agents.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.
